subject: Residency & DPA: CardioPay — APAC pinning, subprocessors, and transient failover
messages:
From: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@cardiopay.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Residency requirements & DPA — CardioPay (APAC)

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal and infosec at CardioPay are reviewing Redwood for a payments pilot and we need to lock down a few items before procurement can sign:

- Strong preference for APAC residency for production inference (user PII + embeddings). Can Redwood commit to an APAC-only placement for our active workload? If not, please describe the exact failure/fallback window and triggers.
- Are there any transient cross-region hops for analytics, telemetry, or batch reprocessing? If yes, what are max durations and notification/approval processes?
- We need a current subprocessor roster (names, roles, region) and whether any subprocessor has access to plaintext data.
- KMS options: do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) in APAC regions? If not, what safeguards do you provide?
- Please share your current DPA (redlineable). CardioPay will propose one short addendum for operator access and transient failover notification SLA.

Can you send the roster and DPA today and propose a short timeline for evidence (SOC2, subprocessor attestations)? Also propose times for a legal+ops 30–45m call on Aug 17.

Attachment: None in this message.

Best,
Sarah Tan
Head of Security Programs
CardioPay
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@cardiopay.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency requirements & DPA — CardioPay (APAC)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and I attached our DPA draft + current subprocessor roster for your review (see attachments). I copied Kim (ops/security) to add a technical timeline.

Summary commitments (we can include in a DPA addendum):
- APAC pinning: We can commit to deploying and serving CardioPay traffic from APAC-only placement for production models you select. That commitment covers storage, inference, and transient caches for active requests.
- Transient failover: We will maintain a conditional failover policy for availability. Typical window for emergency cross-region routing is up to 24 hours for catastrophic region failures (we aim to avoid but must be explicit). Any planned transient crosshop for maintenance will be scheduled with 72h notice and require prior approval for scope >1h.
- Analytics & batch: Background analytics reprocessing and aggregate telemetry may run in other regions; we will not use customer embeddings/PII for analytics without explicit opt-in.
- Subprocessors: roster attached (subprocessor_roster_20260815.csv). None of the listed subprocessors hold long-term plaintext backups for your production inference requests; operator access is logged and audited.
- KMS: We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via our APAC KMS integration for Dedicated/Private plans; hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys with HSM protections. We can discuss a split-KMS model for analytics isolation if needed.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v2.docx (DPA draft), subprocessor_roster_20260815.csv (current roster)

Next steps we propose:
1) CardioPay legal reviews the DPA and marks any redlines — we can receive redlines via DocuSign or tracked comments.
2) Ops sends an evidence packet (SOC2 summary, uptime runbook, audit log snippets) within 2 business days — Kim will follow up with specifics.
3) Schedule legal+ops call Aug 17 10:00–10:45 PT / Aug 17 01:00–01:45 AEST (propose alternate if that conflicts).

If you want the APAC pin to be written into a contract clause (e.g., pinning + temporary-failover carveout) we can add an addendum with the exact triggers/notifications.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@cardiopay.com>

Cc: Legal Team <legal@cardiopay.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency requirements & DPA — CardioPay (APAC)

Vanessa — appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. A few clarifications before our legal team starts redlining:

- Embeddings: are embeddings produced for inference requests stored outside APAC for analytics or model training? We need written confirmation they will remain within APAC unless we opt into analytics.
- Logs: for debugging, do you retain request/response payloads? If so, can we request a no-persistent-logs option for CardioPay (or shorter retention window)?
- Operator access: please confirm whether operator/admin access can be restricted by region and whether access requires MFA plus justification (we expect audit evidence).

We'll aim to have initial redlines by Aug 18 EOD. Please confirm DocuSign path for execution and whether you can accept our addendum on temporary-failover notifications.

Thanks,
Sarah

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Residency requirements & DPA — CardioPay (APAC)

Hi Sarah — Kim from Security/Platform here with the technical commitments and a short ops timeline: 

- Embeddings and inference data store: For the production models you designate we will pin inference and embedding storage to APAC. There is no automatic export of embeddings for model training or analytics unless CardioPay explicitly opts in. We'll include a contractual clause to that effect.
- Short-lived caches / KV: We use in-memory and short-lived KV caches for latency (TTL typically < 5 minutes). Those caches will be colocated in APAC for pinned workloads.
- Transient crosshop: Emergency failover paths exist; policy is: (1) automated cross-region routing only on catastrophic AZ/region loss; (2) maximum transient crosshop duration 24 hours; (3) notification to CardioPay within 30 minutes of detected failover and full post-incident report within 48 hours. Planned maintenance cross-hops require 72h notice and written approval for windows >1 hour.
- Logs & retention: By default we log request/response metadata and error traces. We do not persist full request/response payloads for longer than 7 days in hosted plans unless debugging is enabled. We can offer a no-persistent-logs configuration (truncate payloads on write) for CardioPay; operational impact is that root-cause debugging requires a short-lived opt-in session.
- Operator access: Role-based access controls (RBAC) enforced with MFA — operator sessions are logged and can be scoped by region for Dedicated/Private accounts. We will provide audit samples in the evidence packet.

Ops timeline:
- Evidence packet (SOC2 summary, audit log sample, operator access audit): 2 business days (target Aug 17 COB).
- Final subprocessor roster with access annotations: 2 business days (already attached but will add access notes by Aug 17).
- DPA redline review: we'll triage redlines as they arrive and aim to respond within 48 business hours.

Ben — can you start procurement paperwork and confirm whether the APAC pin needs a milestone in the SOW? Laura — tagging for legal escalation if CardioPay requests a binding region guarantee beyond pinning + transient-failover carveout.

Thanks — happy to join the call on Aug 17 for ops questions.

Kimberly Park
Head of Platform Security Operations
Redwood Inference
